topic: Intervals on the Real Number Line
title: Is 40 Allowed? Intervals Explained Simply | PUC Maths Class 11
description:
A road sign says speed 20 to 40 km/h, and Aarav is riding at exactly 40. Is he inside the limit or just outside it? Maths settles it with one tiny detail: a round bracket or a square bracket. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Maths (NCERT Chapter 1, Sets) we learn intervals on the real number line: open, closed and half open intervals, their length, and intervals that run to infinity.

You will zoom in between 31 and 32 to see that an interval has no gaps, watch a point run to the end of a closed interval and land on 40, then chase the end of an open interval through 39.9, 39.99, 39.999 without ever reaching it. There is a pause-and-think question, a worked example that turns -5 < x ≤ 7 into an interval, the [2, 5] exam trap, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and JEE Main students.

In this video:
0:00 Speed 20 to 40 km/h: is 40 allowed?
0:26 What is an interval?
0:47 Open, closed and half open intervals
1:25 Live: a point runs to the end
1:51 Pause and think: is 2 in (2, 5]?
2:06 Length of an interval
2:18 Intervals that run to infinity
2:39 Worked example: -5 < x ≤ 7
3:14 Exam trap: [2, 5] is not {2, 3, 4, 5}
3:32 Where it is asked
3:45 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
4:21 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode (Ep 8): Union, Intersection and Difference. Two friends' favourite fruits: all of them, the ones they share, and the ones only she likes.
